sex.evidence: Male Wistar rats weighing 300-350g were provided by the Centro de Desenvolvimento de Modelos Experimentais para Medicina e Biologia

dosing.evidence: The following freeze-dried ayahuasca extract doses were utilized: 120, 240 and 480 mg/kg ... administered orally by gavage ... Long-term administration consisted of a daily oral dose for 30 days by gavage.

group_housing.evidence: The animals were housed in group of 5 animals per cage

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12 hour light/dark cycle (lights on at 7:00 a.m.)

assays.assay_description: EPM with two open arms (50×10×1 cm) and two enclosed arms (50×10×40 cm), elevated 50 cm. Rats placed on the center facing an open arm and allowed to move freely for 5 min. Measures: % open arm time, % open arm entries, rearing frequency, head dip frequency.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to move freely for 5 minutes

food_restriction.evidence: No food in apparatus during 5-min EPM test

water_restriction.evidence: No water in apparatus during test

time_to_assay.evidence: Forty-eight hours after the last administration, the subjects were placed on the center of the EPM

outcomes.summary: Long-term ayahuasca administration (120, 240, 480 mg/kg for 30 days) did not affect anxiety-like behaviour in the EPM. No significant differences in % open arm time, % open arm entries, rearing, or head dip frequency.
outcomes.evidence: the one-way ANOVA showed no difference among groups in any parameters investigated

B1_num_measures.evidence: %Open arm time spent, %Open arm entries, Frequency of rearing, Frequency of head dip

B4_ethological.evidence: Frequency of rearing and head dip scored as distinct natural exploratory acts

B5_social.evidence: subjects were placed on the center of the EPM

B6_cognitive.evidence: EPM is an innate anxiety test

B7_automated_classification.evidence: behavior was video recorded; no ML/pose-estimation classifier mentioned

E1_environment_type.evidence: Elevated plus maze with open and enclosed arms

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are apparatus design, not a shelter (definitionally absent)

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM arms are open-ended extensions of central platform, not distinct enclosed compartments

D2_session_duration.evidence: allowed to move freely for 5 minutes

D5_followup.evidence: Forty-eight hours after the last administration

assays.assay_description: Contextual and tone fear conditioning in MED-Associates chamber (30×24×21 cm) with stainless steel grid floor. Background: 5 tone-footshock pairings (80dB, 5kHz, 5s; 1s 0.6mA shock). Foreground: 5 footshocks alone. Tests assess freezing during 300-s re-exposure to training context (CFC), novel context with tone (TFC, Exp 1) or novel context B (Exp 2), and 5 repeated context A sessions on days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35.

setup_restrain.evidence: rats placed individually in chamber and allowed to move freely

food_restriction.evidence: No food in conditioning chamber during test

time_to_assay.evidence: Forty-eight hours after the last administration, the subjects were submitted to ... conditioning chamber

outcomes.summary: Long-term ayahuasca 120 mg/kg increased contextual freezing in both background and foreground fear conditioning paradigms. Effect was specific to training context A (not novel context B), and the elevated freezing relative to control persisted across repeated context A sessions over 35 days. Tone fear conditioning was not selectively affected (pre-CS freezing also elevated at 120 mg/kg, attributed to context generalization).
outcomes.statistics: Exp 1 CFC: F(3,42)=3.8, p=0.01 (Tukey: 120 mg/kg > control). Exp 1 TFC: group F(3,42)=2.76, p=0.05; time F(1,42)=324.8, p≤0.001; interaction F(3,42)=2.05, p=0.12. Exp 2 Context A: t(22)=-2.32, p=0.03; Context B: t(22)=-1.09, p=0.28. Repeated sessions: group F(1,22)=9.4, p<0.001; time F(4,88)=34.4, p<0.001; interaction F(4,88)=1.91, p=0.11.
outcomes.evidence: animals that received the 120mg/kg ayahuasca dose had increased fear responses when compared with the control group in CFC test ... the ayahuasca group maintained the initial difference from the control group

B1_num_measures.evidence: Freezing in CFC, pre-CS freezing in TFC, post-CS freezing in TFC

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: freezing reported as total per 300s session

B4_ethological.evidence: Freezing is conditioned immobility, excluded from ethological behaviours

B6_cognitive.evidence: fear conditioning is a model of associative emotional learning

B7_automated_classification.evidence: freezing scored as complete immobility; no ML classifier mentioned

E3_bedding.evidence: floor consisted of 19 stainless steel rods

E6_spatial.evidence: conditioning chamber is a single compartment; context A vs context B are separate apparatuses used on different days

E7_social_context.evidence: rats placed individually in the chamber

E8_food_water.evidence: no food or water in apparatus

D1_continuity.evidence: Training + CFC (24h) + TFC (48h) + repeated context A sessions on days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35

D3_recording_days.evidence: Training + CFC test + context B + 5 repeated context A sessions (days 7-35) ≈ 8 recording days for Exp 2

D4_baseline.evidence: no pre-drug baseline freezing in same assay

D5_followup.evidence: testing began 48h after last dose and extended to 35 days post-training

assays.assay_description: Spatial version MWM in 200 cm diameter black circular pool with submerged 10 cm platform. Training: 4 trials/day for 5 consecutive days (1 min trial max, 30 s ITI). Probe session: 1 min free swim without platform. Tracked using Noldus EthoVision v7.0. Measures: escape latency across training days and time in target quadrant during probe.

water_restriction.evidence: No drinking water accessible during trial

time_to_assay.evidence: Forty-eight hours after the last administration, the subjects were trained on the MWM

outcomes.summary: Long-term ayahuasca administration (120, 240, 480 mg/kg) did not affect MWM acquisition (latency declined across days for all groups) or probe-test memory (all groups spent more time in target quadrant). No dose-dependent effects on spatial learning.
outcomes.evidence: no group effects [F(3,92) = 0.67; p = 0.57] or group × training period interactions [F(12,368) = 1.11; p = 0.54] were observed in the MWM training

B1_num_measures.evidence: Latency to platform (training) and time in target quadrant (probe)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Across-day training is between-session, not within-session temporal dynamics

B4_ethological.evidence: swimming latency not an ethological behaviour

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Noldus EthoVision v7.0 - position tracking only

E6_spatial.evidence: pool divided into virtual quadrants, single open arena

D1_continuity.evidence: 4 trials/day for 5 consecutive days + probe session

D2_session_duration.evidence: trials capped at 1 min with 30s ITI; probe 1 min

judge_notes: Three assays identified: EPM, Fear Conditioning (combining contextual + tone + foreground/background + repeated extinction sessions as one paradigm under the rubric), and Morris Water Maze.
B1 for EPM scored 2 (4-6 measures: open arm time, open arm entries, rearing, head dip) per modal candidate agreement (qwen, gptoss).
B4 for EPM scored 1 (Yes): rearing and head dipping are natural exploratory acts scored as distinct ethological behaviours, agreeing with glm and gptoss.

E6 for fear conditioning scored 0: training and test happen in same single-compartment chamber; context A vs B are separate apparatuses used on different days, not multi-zone within one session (overriding glm).
D3 for Fear Conditioning scored 2 (8-14 days) covering Exp 2: training day + 24h CFC + 24h context B + 5 repeated sessions on days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 = 8 recording days for this assay.
time_to_assay set to early_2to24h with 2880 min (48 h post-last-dose) per rubric definition; qwen mislabeled bin as short_term_1to7d for 48h, corrected here.
Housing: handling and enrichment_housing kept as not_reported (paper is silent); group housing and standard light cycle explicitly stated.
